quarterly_data.signal: NEW U.S. LAB INVESTMENT, NOT ON THE CALL: Doug said Lam announced a large new lab investment in Oregon about two weeks before the conference, 'which is a key part of a $3 billion investment that we plan to do in lab and engineering capability'. The biggest lab investments in the company are in the U.S. - the Fremont, California headquarters and the large Oregon engineering organization - because that is where Lam does its innovation. Separately, on the wave of new U.S. fab investments Doug said Lam is 'making investments in all of those locations to make sure we have got the engineering capability to support what the customer needs in those locations' - he named only TSMC's Arizona fab as an example ('if they weren't doing there, they would've probably been doing in Taiwan, and we support them the same no matter where they are'). Asked whether Lam's share of U.S. capacity could be higher than its global share, Doug said 'It's consistent.'
quarterly_data.figure: $3 billion investment in lab and engineering capability, including a newly announced Oregon lab

quarterly_data.signal: ENGAGEMENT WITH A NEW-ENTRANT FAB CUSTOMER: asked about the unconventional new fab customers coming to market, Doug would not name the company but confirmed the engagement: 'there's a potential large amount of demand that shows up there. We are deeply engaged already with that specific customer. I have to be careful not talking too much about any one customer, but the engagement there is already in place, and will be.' He added that with a new-type customer 'the opportunity to do more and provide even more for a customer like that is very high, and we're making sure we're very focused on it'. No units, value or timing were given.

2027 SEGMENT RANKING: Ram said that after a 2026 WFE led by DRAM, then leading-edge foundry/logic, then NAND, next year has 'a similar setup in terms of ranking' and is 'still led by DRAM next year, but the gap between leading-edge foundry logic's WFE spend and DRAM is probably a little closer next year. Leading-edge foundry logic is very strong next year.' Asked to handicap foundry versus DRAM, Doug declined to rank them: 'both are going to go quite high, and NAND'. He tied the strength to 3D architecture inflections Lam is levered to - gate-all-around, backside power, advanced packaging TSV and HBM - each gate-all-around and backside-power step worth about $1 billion of incremental SAM per 100,000 wafer starts of capacity.
